summary:
Light-lag is a free, browser-based co-op game in which up to four players design a crewed mission to Mars, then fly it with every message delayed by the real speed of light.

Players plan the mission on NASA’s real 2020 launch window, choosing the rocket, science instruments, power, shielding and radio plan, and balancing mass, power, data and cost. A review board checks the plan before launch. In flight, two players in Houston and two aboard the ship face a solar storm replayed from real data and eleven days of silence while the Sun blocks the radio. Every choice returns as a consequence, and the debrief shows what each decision caused.

The game answers the challenge by turning mission design into an experience you live with, not a checklist that ends at launch. It runs on NASA data: SPICE ephemerides, Deep Space Network passes, DONKI space weather and Curiosity’s radiation measurements.

It matters because the first crews to Mars will live inside this delay. Through one family’s goodnights, Light-lag shows why design decisions are how we protect them.=
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Light-lag follows NASA's own lifecycle: design, review, flight, debrief. Two players sit in Houston at Lantern Control (the Flight Director and the Mission Scientist) and two aboard Meridian-1 (Commander Imani Reyes and Flight Engineer Daniel Okafor, with two more crew played by AI). Any seat nobody takes is played by AI, so one person can play alone.

The team first designs the mission in nine steps: the objective and science payload, the launch date on a real porkchop plot of the 2020 window, the rocket, the solar array and battery, the storm shelter, the radio plan, and what TERN, the ship's AI, may do without asking. Four budgets (mass, power, data and cost) must close with margin. A Flight Readiness Review of five reviewers then checks the design against written thresholds, each cited or labelled MODEL. A pass can carry liens, accepted risks that come back in flight; a failure slips the launch date.

Then they fly it in eight scenes from launch to the October 2021 solar conjunction. Every message waits out the true one-way light time: 6.1 seconds on Day 5, 172 seconds on Day 98, almost 22 minutes at conjunction. A real solar flare is replayed, and for eleven days the Sun blocks everything. A debrief rebuilds the mission as chains of decision, event and outcome. Every mission is its own room with a four-letter code, so several teams can play at once.

HOW IT WORKS

One Python server runs an authoritative universe clock and an event queue. Positions come from NASA/JPL SPICE ephemerides; the fictional ship's trajectory is written into its own SPICE file, so its light time is computed exactly like a real spacecraft's. Every message is a delay-tolerant network bundle delivered at transmit time plus light time, and only when a Deep Space Network antenna can hear the ship. Earth and the ship keep separate knowledge, so Houston always sees the past. The review board, the design-to-flight callouts and their counterfactuals are deterministic and re-run the same model with the other choice; every assumption is labelled MODEL on screen. Crew members track fatigue, stress, trust and morale. TERN's decisions come from a deterministic policy engine that acts alone when harm would arrive before Earth's answer could; a language model only phrases its words.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

Students and the public learn real mission trade-offs by living with them: launch windows, mass and power margins, radiation shielding, antenna time, and why a crew at Mars cannot wait for Houston. The story of Imani and her seven-year-old daughter Lila makes the physics personal without changing a number.

WHAT WE HOPE TO ACHIEVE

A classroom or museum activity where a group designs a mission, argues about margins, and then feels each decision come back at the speed of light.

TOOLS, LANGUAGES AND HARDWARE

Python 3.11 with FastAPI, Uvicorn, SpiceyPy, NumPy, PyYAML, httpx, ONNX Runtime and pytest (124 automated tests). Browser clients in plain JavaScript modules with three.js; no build step. A small autoencoder trained with PyTorch and exported to ONNX flags telemetry anomalies onboard. Optional local open-weight language models through Ollama. Hosting on a computer behind a Cloudflare Tunnel, with Heroku as backup. Runs offline on a laptop; players join from phones or other computers on the same network.

CREATIVE CHOICES

Silence is a feature: during conjunction the sound drops to room tone. The family story is hand-written and never scored. We never slow light down: the whole universe runs ten times faster, so every event keeps its true causal order.
